notes.title: Community Update #2
notes.content:
Greetings, survivors!

We are happy to present to you a new addition to the Siege Survival: Gloria Victis - the final iteration of Dynamic Events for both scenarios!

We heard your feedback, where you were pointing that it would be great to have some more diversity between each gameplay, and if the game would better react to your actions and needs. So we deliver!

Additionally, we are introducing two new challenges for the Lost Caravan scenario, as well as the New Game + mode for it. You can now try yourself in a race against time or survive the siege of caravanserai under the pressure of a never-ending sandstorm. NG+ gives you the same opportunities that we already have for the Siege of Edring scenario - you can adjust the gameplay to your liking!

The game, especially the second scenario, receives a lot of Quality of Life changes, which will enhance your experience, as well as some bug fixes and improvements, to ensure the best possible impressions from your time spent in the game.

Check the details below, and see you on the fortress's walls!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/baa3ee8da75a6eb7034b11910fc8b87bc4be194b.jpg[/img]
[i]Have you found the old battlefield already? There are tons of armanent there![/i]

[h2]Dynamic events[/h2]

[i]Dynamic Events[/i] is a system conjugated with the game autobalancer system, which is modifying the gameplay as you play and introduces more variety in the game, basing on various circumstances. From now on, in both scenarios, you may face events that will impact your gameplay.

The events will be shown from time to time at the beginning of the castle stage and will be based on your previous actions, choices, and status of your crew or Bastion. They can have a positive or negative impact, but can also add extra narration to the story, giving you even more insight into the events happening in your surrounding. They can also be used to forecast some changes in the game world like you were already able to see in the Lost Caravan scenario, where the system has been used to predict the beginning and end of the sandstorm.

We believe this fine addition will improve your feelings and add an extra layer to the playthroughs, creating a more coherent vision of the stories and gameplay. Be sure to leave your feedback on our Socials, Steam Hub, or reviews! We are thankful for your opinions!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/92525c218034fc5eecee1208bfed33bb4aa7177d.jpg[/img]
[i]Example of one of the events you can now experience in the game.[/i]

[h2]Quality of life[/h2]
[list]
[*]All characters in-game received short stories that will show at game summary, telling their further history after the siege.
[*]Added a new trader in the Lost Caravan scenario.
[*]Economy and difficulty balance tweaks for the Lost Caravan scenario.
[*]Added two new challenges and New Game + mode for the Lost Caravan Scenario
[*]Added Dynamic Events to both scenarios.
[*]New illustrations for various events.
[*]Improved the AI: guards are now walking instead of running toward the player when the time on scavenging ends.
[*]Improved guard's reaction to hearing a noise.
[*]Added a special sergeant guard in the Lost Caravan scenario which can drop some useful loot.[/list]
[h2]Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*]Fixed an issue preventing the player from stopping fire of a passive crafting building (i.e. Garden Plot) after it was set aflame at the moment when the passive crafting was being prepared.
[*]Fixed an issue causing characters to meet themselves in events outside the castle in the Lost Caravan scenario.
[*]Fixed an issue causing some of the map markers were not working properly.
[*]Fixed all known issues causing cow carcasses to hang on the models of the buildings where they were impossible to remove.
[*]Fixed an issue causing the game summary screen was not counting everything correctly.
[*]Multiple spelling and color-coding fixes in text events.[/list]

notes.title: New scenario is out!
notes.content:
Greetings survivors!

As we promised just a few weeks ago, we decided to make some improvements to the game based on your feedback. In your reviews and posts across our social channels, we found a lot of positive opinions about the game -  but also a lot of requests to introduce more content, to keep the joy of playing the game for longer, in a unique setting - since so many of you wanted to play more!

A new scenario, named the ‘Lost Caravan’ tells the story of a caravan crew - ambushed and besieged inside a caravanserai on a harsh southern desert. You will face new challenges, meet new characters and test your time and resource management skills in a new economy, customised for the new setting.

Today's update also includes a new system for morning events - which we announced earlier - that is already included in a new scenario and will be implemented in the base scenario soon, because we wanted to reserve some more time to make it even better.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/8a338de51d093e47b6fc86948a0f8e79e7f24927.png[/img]

[h2]New scenario - Lost caravan[/h2]

The new story takes place two years after the end of the Siege of Edring. A group of survivors - attacked by the advancing enemy -  is trapped inside an abandoned caravanserai and are making a last stand, facing not only the enemy attacks but also scorching weather and unexpected deadly danger, relentlessly rolling over the desert.

Your task will be escaping the trap, in a limited amount of time, while holding the walls and preparing an escape route. 

The new scenario will be unlocked to everyone who reached or will reach the seventh day in the Siege of Edring scenario. It will ensure more hours of gameplay and will be a unique experience. We hope you will like it!

[h3]New mechanic - Overheat[/h3]

The unforgiving southern sun is a threat in itself. Since - in the new scenario - you are managing your camp during the night when it is cooler, and scavenging during the day when the enemies are less active because of the heat; but you need to avoid staying outside too long, otherwise you will get sick from the heat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/ae9090eca14b0a1de599fbd386e0552bb3687212.png[/img]

[h3]New weather - Sandstorm[/h3]

Every few days a sandstorm will hit the area which will have an impact on gameplay; while the biting dust - choking throats and lungs – will increase your chances of getting sick, it will also reduce visibility for both you and your enemies when scavenging. It is a risk to go outside since your orientation will be much less efficient. But taking such risk can be sometimes needed (or at least very profitable).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/9d0c2f28b99bb09ce7ac92cc832f2f150bbc695f.png[/img]

[h3]Community update #2 announced![/h3]

In two weeks from now, after gathering your feedback about the new scenario, we will prepare an update that will include balance changes, morning events to the Edring Siege, and some of the convenience improvements we are working on. We wanted to share the new scenario with you as soon as possible and we are already working on the challenges and New Game + mode for "Lost Caravan", which will also be introduced in the upcoming update.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/f9032b814d414151c91b27afaef72fbb1dc6e871.png[/img]

We are grateful for your support and cheering for us! Thank you for your patience and trust, and we hope you will have a lot of fun with the new story!

/ Siege Survival Team

notes.title: Post release summary and roadmap for upcoming weeks!
notes.content:
Greetings, survivors!

It's been a week since the release of Siege Survival and we are very happy to see that you like the game and see its potential. We can't express enough how happy we were to see the game reaching the top 6 in bestsellers this week and still holding on the top of the New and Trending Steam chart with a score of over 80% positive reviews!

It is heartwarming to see so many positive reviews praising the gameplay, unique setting, and bug-free experience, and we are honored that you found a place for us in your hearts!

We are reading all reviews, topics on forums, and messages sent to us through our socials. We see you like the game's mechanics and the story of Edring's Last Stand a lot. Also, the experienced players find it enjoyable to face the available Challenges and experiment with New Game Plus feature which lets you adjust your next gameplay even more. However, by reading your reviews it becomes clear to us that most of you would like to see more unique content in the game.

We are a small indie team that was always putting our Community first before anything else, and to be close with the Community is one of the most precious things for us. We are super thankful for your feedback! We are always here for you and we can assure you that we are working already and will work further on the game to introduce a lot of improvements and additional content. 

To make our pledge official, we are happy to share the post-release roadmap that will explain what is the plan for the upcoming weeks for Siege Survival.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/7b24cad3d910273f2a61061cc109efc11d44c444.png[/img]

[h3]Quality of Life and Editor Funcionality[/h3]

Later this very week, you can expect an update that will contain some more Quality of Life changes and improvements, including some ideas suggested by the Community (compass rose on the UI while scavenging!). We will also fix some small bugs with guards AI and balance the number of guards a little on the highest alert level.

In addition to that, we are continuing our work on Siege Editor - the complex tool that we used to create the "Edring's Last Stand" scenario and you can already use to make your own stories! As we are working on its documentation right now, we are still adding new features that will allow you to have more tools to differ your own creations. We also starting cooperation with some pro modders communities so you can expect to see their contribution and mod contests in the future. In the upcoming update, you will be able to access enemy creator to change the guard's stats, loot, and visuals, and animal room system, which will help you to set up the animal's needs and products.

[h3]Dynamic Events[/h3]

We know, that the castle gameplay is fun when it comes to the mechanics of building, crafting, and micromanaging your castle crew. But we also know, that the late stages of the game can become slightly repetitive and there is too little going on story-wise in the castle. We want to improve that by adding dynamic events, conjugated with our auto balancer system. Those events will be randomly generated and will happen in the morning or during the day in the day phase. They will provide some more storytelling and some more positive and negative modifications that will impact your gameplay. We hope those will be a great addition to the game and improve your experience.

[h3]New desert scenario[/h3]

As you clearly said as a Community, that you want more content, we will deliver. We are creating a new scenario for Siege Survival, titled "Lost caravan". Its action will take place in the far south, in dessert areas near the trade route between Sangmar Empire and the Central Sea which is imperial traders' main path for export and import goods with other nations. We will not spoil more details about the story yet, but we can say that the gameplay will be totally different and the goals you would need to achieve to win the scenario will also be different. We hope you will like it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/7559b0fe00721e180baa3717ed5a73ddffbdabe4.jpg[/img]
[I]What a nice wide screenshot from [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2495630120]Mr. Lucky Pants[/url]! Thank you for that capture![/i]


And this would be all for today. See you later this week and take care!
/ Siege Survival Team

notes.title: Work in progress insight, new gameplay, and new trailer!
notes.content:
Greetings, Survivors!

We have great news for you!

Today is a day when we can share with you the progress of the game development and show you how the game changed in recent months. We heard your feedback and we are thankful for your suggestions which helped us a lot to make Siege Survival even better!

To put you in the proper mood, before telling you some more, let's watch our new "Siege of Edring" trailer first. We hope you'll like it!
[previewyoutube=phcwvFyofuk;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Short Work In Progress Summary[/h3]

The months between releasing the Demo and today were very busy for us since we received tons of feedback worth addressing and continued our work on extending and upgrading existing systems. Among many things done, we reworked scavenge guards, to make the mechanics related to them more player-friendly. We remade the tutorial system to make them more informative and clear. Finished the work on the map system to make it better visually and more useful in-game. We created a set of tools that will help you plan your gameplay and get knowledge about the possible ways to survive, like showing lists of available buildings and recipes related to them. And we also introduced a time management system to give players the possibility to slow down or speed up the time in the castle.

[h3]Updated Demo[/h3]

On that occasion, we are giving you the updated Demo version with all the improved features and changes to allow you to check them by yourselves. Since the core game code of the game has been changed due to the improvements and optimization, saves that were made before today's update will not work, you have to start a new game to experience the new build. We are aware that it may be small trouble but with such deep and extensive changes, it was absolutely justified to sacrifice compatibility between game versions. We hope this small inconvenience will be balanced with your refreshed game experience and you will be blown away by the progress we made!

[h3]Survive the siege with your favorite content creators![/h3]

To spread the word about the game in the world we decided to share an extended preview version of the game to media and content creators. You can check a special version of the gameplay today and in the following days by visiting some YouTubers and Streamers. The Preview version of the game is a week longer than the Demo and has access to parts of the city, buildings, recipes, and characters not shown anywhere before! If after playing the new Demo you have to know what is the next chapter of the story, be sure to look for videos and content on Youtube and Twitch! 

We also prepared our short narrated video showing some gameplay after day 7, so it would be great if you could leave some love for the game in the comments and a thumb up if you like the changes! 
[previewyoutube=XQRaFDWxwds;full][/previewyoutube]

And that would be all for now. We are continuing our work and preparing for the release. If you have any questions or suggestions, do not hesitate to drop them here in our Community Hub!

Play the new Demo, add the game to your Wishlist, follow Siege Survival on [url=https://www.facebook.com/SiegeSurvivalGloriaVictis]Facebook[/url] and [url=https://twitter.com/SiegeSurvival]Twitter[/url], and continue being awesome!

[i]Much love and stay safe!
Siege Survival Developers Team[/i]

We’re working hard to make Siege Survival even better, so we are thankful for your understanding, regarding our decision to allocate some more time before release.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/0c0a8daee062ae578c073a01cfb0e11f8822318b.png[/img]

Instead of giving you a long list of things we added, changed, updated, and improved, we thought it will be better to give you a sample of our work and let you compare the changes and improvements for yourselves, although we’ve outlined some of the significant changes below.

[h2]Updated Prologue Build for the upcoming Steam Game Festival![/h2]

In the prologue, you’ll play through the beginning of the main story and see for yourself all the improvements and changes in the game, many as a result of your feedback and suggestions. You’ll find some significant user interface improvements and user experience changes in the updated prologue demo. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/72de3df08a2992d723779322571422fb2fc96206.png[/img]

We extended the building mechanics, adding the ability to cancel building orders and dismantle standing buildings which allows you to retrieve some of the materials used in its construction.

The guards’ AI is now more balanced, so you’ll find it easier to perform a sneak attack while holding a weapon and approaching from behind. However, they are now more efficient when searching and will now use arrows if they cannot catch up to your character.

Scavenge features, including movement and fighting, became more intuitive and user friendly since we added some safeguards to ensure players will not get punished too much for making mistakes. But remember, patience is a virtue and the enemy guards are not your friends. 

The game economy has been rebalanced, with some changes to what items are and are not available, along with some amendments making some more suited to the vision and immersion in the game. 

We added an excellent map extension that will show you supplies available in each city district which will help you plan your scavenging routes more effectively before going out. We also reworked the night actions screen, allowing you to select which items you need on each mission more intuitively and making them easier to remember.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38218374/75dce15737e8e015243800f894bb260a5f0f133b.png[/img]

Some of the changes we’ve made are in parts of the game beyond the demo since many of the game mechanics and features are introduced later, but we hope you like what you see so far and we’re working hard to ensure the final release will be all we want it to be and more.

Also, we are happy to announce...

We had a lot of positive feedback on the music within the game, so you’ll be pleased to hear that the soundtrack of Siege Survival: Gloria Victis will be available as a DLC and you can wishlist this already.

The soundtrack contains 15 breathtaking tracks composed and recorded by the acclaimed Marcin Przybyłowicz and Magdalena Urbańska. We hope you will find joy in listening to them and appreciate them as much as we do. Be sure to add the Soundtrack DLC to your wishlist!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1407360/Siege_Survival_Gloria_Victis_Soundtrack/

Thank you once again for your support and we hope you will enjoy playing the new Prologue build and like the improvements. If you have any questions, be sure to reach us here on Steam forums or [url=https://twitter.com/SiegeSurvival/status/1323993059315601408]our Socials[/url] and a dedicated Siege Survival section on the [url=https://discord.gg/gQuGkH3]Official Gloria Victis Discord server[/url]!

notes.title: Work in progress insight - final stretch!
notes.content:
Greetings Survivors!

Those ware very busy weeks for Siege Survival crew. We were mentioned on prestige gaming industry events, like in Digital Dragons and #PAXEGX global online events. We addressed your feedback from the Prologue and made countless improvements and bugfixes for the final game. We introduced the very last planned features, new stories and events, new playable and NPC characters, prepared new game + sandbox, cloud save system and finally – we hit 50 000 wishlists milestone!

On that occasion, I think it would be nice to give you some details about the progress we made. We are working hard on the game, and we would like to polish the game as good as we could. So, without further ado, lets jump straight to it.

[h2]New Features[/h2]

First things first, we'd like to thank all our players for all the extensive feedback we've received from the Prologue! It greatly helped us to get our priorities right, and gave us the very best confidence that the last few features we're going to add are on spot.

We introduced a lot of new features to extend the gameplay possibilities of the game, as an example adding a stationary trebuchet in the castle – an endgame interactive building that will allow you to launch deadly projectiles to enemies and turn the tide. But first, you would need to do some things to bring that old war engine back to life. 

You will be able to repair the trebuchet in the midgame. We want to give the player a time to learn basic game mechanics, develop the infrastructure and prepare for harder battles before the game will introduce new layers and options that extend gameplay.

And that is not all! Since the trebuchet is such a powerful weapon, using it effectively will require your best dedication in terms of the resources, time and characters management. But with what a reward! Had you prepared pots to make the base of your devastating flaming projectiles, you’re ready to venture out for the place where tar can be collected. Then, all you have to do after returning with your ammunition back to the castle is to scout enemy lines to make your trebuchet shots even more deadly… and fire at will!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38218374/10fdf4aa4db3a7ee983789e3a2c98c475a8d9ece.gif[/img]
[i]You can find extended gif in better quality [url=https://gyazo.com/e7e4b01f54b846a3a978c332d61dc9ec]here [/url][/i]

[h2]Economy[/h2]

The well balanced, intuitive and fair economy is crucial in such the resources and time management games as Siege Survival is. We heard your feedback: we improved and extended a huge part of the in-game economy, adjusting it to the phasing of the game as well to old and new tasks and challenges you will face during gameplay. 

In the final game, it will be more player dependant how you will cover the needs of your castle crew and the Bastion. Players will be able to adjust the flexible gameplay to their demands so everyone –  hardcore and casual players  – will get the best game experience.

Building a harmonious and self-sufficient economic base is still a challenge, but looking at all facilities working well for the common purpose is a unique experience of its kind.

[h2]Immersion[/h2]

Another aspect of the game we received a lot of feedback from you was the immersion. We want you to identify with ingame civilians and soldiers, establish a relationship with them and feel the full range of emotions while playing Siege Survival.

First, we took care of the visual and sound setting of the game. We added new tracks, sounds, made Edring City more influencing on emotions and senses. Added more fire, smoke, corpses, crows and other things that will make night scavenge more immersive, so you will feel, that those streets ran red with blood just a few days ago, citizens ran away or hid from the raiders and everyone who has left is counting on you to hold the last stand.

Another part that was reported by you was a fact, that soldiers were stationed in another part of the castle, behind another wall, behind the bridge and three gates. So, we moved the fight under your walls. Bastion is now an integral part of the castle you have as your base, and enemies are now hitting your gate. This increases the sense of responsibility and greatly helps to make you feel being under siege.

There are more changes that will help immersion, like improvement of the fighting system if you decide to take your chances in fighting one of the enemies at night, adding another type of bombardment you will need to take care off (cow corpses thrown inside the walls spreading disease!) or adding even more moral choices in the events and a lot of improvements. All these improvements add to the overall experience created by both the game's mechanics and the emotional layer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38218374/67db24a27a775a99cb28815edc2749e583ddedd1.png[/img]
[i]You can see here some buildings you have never seen before: Rat Trap, Water Collector, Garden Plot and mentioned earlier - Trebuchet![/i]

[h2]Scenario Editor[/h2]

Adjusting the game to your demands and needs using the New Game + feature is one thing, but how about the possibility of creating the entirely new and unique scenarios? How great would it be to make your events, create your characters with unique traits, have the power to change the game economy and loot, create your buildings and crafting recipes or set up the ultimate challenge for other players changing and adjusting battles difficulty?

Well, you will be able to do that thanks to the integrated scenario editor that we created and keep using while we’re creating the default scenario! It gives almost infinite options – for us, and for you! – to create new exciting stories, meet new characters and share your very own vision of the Siege Survival with everyone! The fun will be endless, and we are looking forward to seeing your ideas and dreams reforged into great mods and standalone scenarios.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38218374/5df1d96fc4758f4b9438f54edec7f92caec58c02.png[/img]
[i]Screenshot showing the text event editor tab in Siege Survival Scenario Editor![/i]

[h2]Wishlist challenge – Additional translation[/h2]

And the last but not least – we have a pleasure to announce that we just hit the 50,000 Wishlist milestone! We’d like to thank you from the bottom of our hearts for your support, feedback and encouragement. This wouldn’t be done without you!

As it’s been announced, reaching this milestone means that we will translate the game to a new language chosen by the Community. People across the world have spoken and the vote result is... German! This language received the most votes and we already started to look for translators to add German localization to the game. 

[b]Here is the percentage of votes:[/b]
[list]
[*] 54% – German
[*] 15% – Spanish
[*] 10% – Italian
[*] 8% – Portuguese
[*] 7% – Japanese
[*] 3% – Swedish
[*] 2% – Dutch
[*] 1% – Korean
[/list]
[h2]What is the plan for the nearest future?[/h2]

Despite our honest will to share the game with you as soon as possible, the game release may be delayed a little because of various reasons. We are a small indie studio, and we want to make Siege Survival the best possible experience for you. That is why we would like to reserve a little more time to polish and optimize the game even better before the release.

We can't stress it enough to thank you enough for your support, feedback and cheering. We are honoured to be able to create and be part of such a wonderful community.

Stay tuned and remember:
These walls will not fall!

notes.title: The final stretch before releasing Prologue!
notes.content:
Greetings, Survivors!

Tomorrow you will be able to check the Siege Survival Prologue by yourselves!
We already told you about daytime sieges you will be able to actively stand against, new characters and traders you will be able to find while scavenging.

By the way, how do you like our new logo?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/41b715090bc2967908e11fd80af69118d6e5fbfa.jpg[/img]

Today, we will tell you some more about the background work we are doing for the final version of the game:

[h3]Save system[/h3]

We received a lot of feedback that the game may need a save system, and there is no way to keep your progress in Demo to get back to the game later in the day. Of course, such a system was planned for the final game, but we pushed ourselves an extra mile and we are proud to announce that you will be able to save your gameplay already in Prologue. Since Prologue is a little longer than the Demo, it may be a useful feature, and we will be also happy to test it with you to check if everything is working properly.

Every gameplay you will start will be automatically saved on the start of each day. And for every session, you will be able to load the last two mornings to fix any potential mistakes you made in the day or try some different route in a text event for an example.

We are also working on a system of saves compatibility between game versions and in addition to that – cloud save – so we will do our best to not lose your progress when we decide to drop a huge update with a lot of backend changes or you will be playing the game on the other side of the world without your personal computer around. 

[h3]New Game Plus[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/28ab7b438a5958b6c93c87b86ddc614addab35ef.jpg[/img]

Most of you may remember that one of our wishlist challenge rewards was New Game + system, that will allow you to change your gameplay in various parts of the game.

So, we can already show you some sneak peeks and tell you what you will be able to change to make Siege Survival sandbox experience adjusted to your demands.

After reaching a certain day in the game, you will be able to start a new adventure with adjustable change. The difficulty of battles will allow you to face more challenging battles and will put more focus on Bastion. Scavenge difficulty will change base alert level and will spawn more or fewer guards at night which will impact your ability to gather resources undetected.

You will also have the option to change the game length and frequency of battles and also set up starting resources and how many of them will be spawned in the occupied city. 

Weather is another important thing because in Siege Survival there will not always be enough water to find and you may be dependent on a water collector that is collecting morning dew and rainwater. It is important to have some stored, because you may even face drought on higher difficulties. 

Last but not least, you can pick characters you want to play with. Each of them has different background stories and unique hidden skills that are making them more or less efficient in some aspects. Some of them will be stronger so they will have more space in their backpacks, some will search for supplies faster or will be more skilled in handling weapons.

The best part of picking characters is that you will need to find them in your gameplay to unlock them for new adventures, so it will be a lot of fun to find all available playable characters!

You can also see on the screenshot above that we are preparing Iron mode – mode for the most demanding and challenge-hungry players that will not allow you to move back and load saved game  – you will have one try and if you lose the game, it will be final.

Stay tuned!

That is all for today, we will move on to putting the last polish touches on the Prologue and we can't wait for your feedback! Also, we would like to invite you to check previous Journals that you might have missed!

Greetings, Survivors!

We’re proud to announce the reveal of Siege Survival: Gloria Victis Prologue! This standalone, Free-To-Play application will introduce you to the story we want to share with you in the game, and give you a taste of improved ingame features and mechanics!

If you’ve played the Demo during Steam Summer Festival, you absolutely must try this version too, as here you’ll find a lot of brand new features, even more challenges, and a countless improvements that we‘ve made after receiving so much of the players’ feedback!

The Prologue will contain the first 7 days (moar than in demo!) of gameplay, letting you learn the dramatic story of the citizens of Edring, and the game’s unique mechanics, even better. You’ll meet new characters, actively help in the defense of Bastion during day time battles (woohoo!), trade with shady merchants, and sneak your way to crucial supplies during night weaving around deadly – and much smarter! – enemy guards.

But let’s break that down, feature by feature, to give you an insight into huge work we’ve already done, and we keep continuing:

[h2]Battles![/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/091c865e31490bbdc294634a681c330e678c06c5.jpg[/img]

We’ve received hundreds of the feedback tickets from the Demo players – it was amazing to see how much fun you’ve got in the game! But there was one specific element that’s been often indicated as one that needs more love:

[b]Battles.[/b]

The overnight assaults made their job of justifying our position as civilians in the besieged castle, and the Bastion’s demand for supplies created a lot of gameplay challenges. But your feedback clearly said that the nighttime battles haven’t been immersive enough and that it’d be better if they had more impact on us, behind the second line of the defense. 

[h3]And here we are, bringing to you what you’ve wanted, needed and asked for![/h3]

Long story short, the invaders have found out that it’s easier to attack castle walls in daylight (seems smart, you must admit, as they rather haven’t brought the night vision for the raid), so they rescheduled their attacks and they will rush at your castle during the day! During attacks, they will:
[list][*]Shoot flaming arrows to set your building on fire and hurt your characters,
[*]Launch deadly stones that will break buildings and defenders’ hearts (even literally, if you dared to stand in one place),
[*]And send (airborne) cow corpses that will spread disease among your people.[/list]

You will need to boil hot tar to hold the gate, repair broken armament to keep soldiers’ defense abilities, and after battle – you will need to find or craft new supplies, arrows, and food to hold your last stand, until the awaited relief comes. You will also need to take care of wounded soldiers, help them patch holes in the walls, and provide psychological care for your people (Ok, I am joking with that one actually). Basically, sieges will look more or less like this:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/954ec262175998c67b15d0c4365b099453bd2158.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/79a8b8bf76937968765cedc4608251105a501d53.gif[/img]

notes.title: Dev Journal #7 - What do I want to build?
notes.content:
In the last [b]Dev Journal #6[/b] we familiarized you with [b]wood and what you can do with it[/b].

Now I want to talk a bit about the things, you can build in [u]Gloria Victis: Siege[/u]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/9b304ae46c2e1d6f43bd004ea82c10fcd6c8b1c8.png[/img]

One of the most important aspects of every survival game is [b]resource management[/b]. The most obvious one is [b]food[/b], the second one is the [b]materials[/b].

Your most basic ones will be [b]wood, firewood, quality wood, cloth, animal parts, “materials” and straws[/b]. Of course, after some time, you’ll get access to [b]iron bars[/b] and more [i]advanced[/i] things. For now, we’ll focus on the basics!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/96c60344c2d9b9239fe166de4601355b649c16cd.png[/img]

We talked about wood and things you can do with it in a [b]previous Dev Journal[/b]. Cloth, materials and straws can be found in the debris of the city and, at the beginning of the game - in the castle.
Animal parts can be created from carcases and found in the city. And if you manage to starve your chickens…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/bf4d7c740f16bce29e374b81fa2b02bb982b1f6d.jpg[/img]

At the beginning you’ll only be able to build some simple stuff - stump, where you can craft firewood or quality wood, butchers table to disassemble animal carcasses or workshop, where you can craft some simple tools. All the things you will build [b]can be further upgraded[/b] allowing you to create more and more cool things in your castle.

[b]BUT [/b]you still need to [b]scavenge [/b]and [b]look around the ruined city[/b], for things you can salvage. [b]Make choices.[/b] Will you [b]help [/b]the old man, or will you [b]steal [/b]everything he has and leave him to [i]die[/i]?

[h2]More about it in next Dev Journal #8![/h2]

notes.title: Dev Journal #6 - Wood you kindly?
notes.content:
[h1]Greetings citizen![/h1]

In [b]last week's Dev Journal[/b] you could learn about [b]food and how its spoilage[/b]. For most of the provision, you’ll need the most basic thing every Medieval Times person had - [b]wood[/b]. Without it, you won’t be able to cook your meal, warm yourself up or build most of the things.

That’s why this will be one of the [b]most important resources[/b] throughout the whole game. The main problem will be the [i]scarcity [/i]of it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/f6b1e3982ba562c1ed10c48db6a8611aea68a4e3.jpg[/img]

Enough with the puns.

The game will take place in the castle and the vicinity of it, therefore [b]there won’t be a lot of trees[/b]. You can try to go further away from the castle, but do you really want to cut down the tree in the middle of a night, during a siege when there are enemy patrols around the city?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/1240e9bb0eee45c21a8953ef9da4cb2e014ef2e7.jpg[/img]

I’m sure, that’s a terrible idea from my point of view but, hey! That’s your story!

Where was I? Oh, right.

The most basic resource will be wood. You'll be able to find it in the ruined buildings or debris scattered around the city. It can be chopped to create [b]firewood [/b]or [b]craftwood[/b].

Both of them will be your [b]biggest friend[/b] during your play through in [b]Gloria Victis: Siege.[/b] Resource management is [b]crucial [/b]in every survival game. Should I build more beds for my citizens? Or maybe cook one more meal, so they’ll be full for a longer period? That’s the question you will ask yourself many, many times in a variety of days during the siege.

Firewood and craftwood can be created with a [b]Stump [/b]- one of the first things you’ll probably build during your second day.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/df7b5fb37efe424a54072db7a529f45a3e4c0737.jpg[/img]

Then what? We already talked about [b]cooking food[/b], so our next topic will be [b]building[/b]. You know about a Stump. How about I tell you about some of the [b]first buildings you’ll probably create[/b]?

[h3]That will be the topic of our next DevJournal![/h3]

notes.title: Dev Journal #5 - Best before date is a challenge, not a limit.
notes.content:
[h1]Hello Community![/h1]

My name is [b]Liq [/b]and this is another [b]Gloria Victis: Siege Dev Journal[/b].

Last week we talked about [b]Perks [/b]and how diverse Middle Ages society were. Everything we talked about so far is connected with the most important thing in every survival game - [b]resources[/b]. Today, we would like to give you some [b]basic knowledge regarding the food and its spoilage[/b].

[b]Question of The Week is - [i]If it smells strange, can I still eat it?[/i][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/c66711d33781017e95836ddb6a565a389abd731f.jpg[/img]

Like in the everyday world, milk can go [b]rancid[/b], vegetables can get [b]mouldy[/b], meat can [b]rot [/b]- food can go [b]bad[/b]. In [b]Gloria Victis: Siege[/b], [i]there’s not much of a difference[/i]. Of course, in the Middle Ages, there are [b]no fridges[/b] you know today, therefore it will go bad [b]quickly[/b].

At the start of the game, all food will be fresh and then spoil after some time. It depends on you, how quickly you will find it. Your everyday food will be vegetables. After some time you will be able to grow them inside the castle, on the courtyard. [b]How quickly will it go bad?[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/6bc1b66c48b493704fc3eca53170850b3321a183.gif[/img]

Depends on the product. Eggs, meat and MRE… I mean cooked meals will [b]take some time to rot[/b] or mouldy. Vegetables? Day or two. Why that quickly? This is the dream of bio-products enthusiasts. Fresh, with no preservatives, artificial fertilizer nor plant spraying. Therefore, you should not gather a lot of short shelf-life products.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/436e203606982f7d81fb27a92c1f716a7179b13f.gif[/img]

But, what happens to the rotten food? [b]Can I still eat it?[/b] In the real world? Kinda, but we really do not encourage this way of life. But you can still give it to the pigs or [b]create fertilizers[/b] with it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/9774cf25e01390b58327941e41a7e64fa0023077.jpg[/img]

And there it is. Thank you very much for reading this [b]DevJournal [/b]and stay tuned for next Thursday, when we will talk about [b]wood [/b]and why this is the second most important resource in [b]Gloria Victis: Siege.[/b]

[h1]Cheers![/h1]

notes.title: Dev Journal #4 - Perky Perks
notes.content:
[h1]Greetings survivors![/h1]

Welcome to another [b]Thursday Dev Journal[/b].

Last week we gave you an insight into the basics of scavenging in a besieged city. What you should look for, what decisions can you make and why should you be quiet during your scavenger hunt. We’ve barely scratched the surface of [b]perks and how they can help you during your play through[/b].

Therefore, this will be the main topic of this Journal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/97a1bbd09e91f6319cf216c7f83368bf629bc7f4.jpg[/img]

Through perks, we'd like to show you [b]how multi-layered and divided the Medieval society has been[/b], which was very stratified and diverse. That’s why you could find a brawny sailor who is also very superstitious and timid.

That’s right – [b]not every perk will be a positive one[/b]. Just like in real life, your survivors will [b]have their flaws and strengths[/b]. Some of perks will be their personal feats, unique for each for them, while the others will come as a side-effect of being a part of a particular social layer.

A blacksmith, as you can suppose, will be strong and brave, even if narrow minded at times. Monk will excel at crafting various medicaments and guide the remaining survivors with his unshaken moral compass. But [b]not everything is black or white, and neither it was in the Middle Ages[/b]. You’ll meet other people in the ruins of the fallen city, knowing only as much as that this person is a noble and this one is a peasant, or that this man managed to defeat the invader with his bare hands to protect his family.

It’s one of the situations where [b]Gloria Victis: Siege[/b] will put you on your toes. You’ll have to make a choice if the person you’ve just met [b]is going to help you[/b], or rather [b]will add to the hardships of surviving[/b] an invasion?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/caa3a574427915a8036fc4cd08370e292b5d4517.png[/img]

One of the most [b]obvious perks[/b] is [b]how many supplies each survivor can carry[/b] during the overnight expeditions to the city ruins. It’s also one of the [b]easiest to notice[/b], since you’ll make a choice who’s going to scavenge every night – depending on the numbers of your survivors, of course.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/c310b79e1da5d68cd8d935952f96b35d467669f3.gif[/img]

[b]How will you craft your story[/b]? Will you try to search every box in the city? Find every encounter? Or maybe hoard everything you can find? Just be careful! [b]Food, like in real life, will decay after some time. [/b]

[b]How long will it take and what can you do to preserve it? This will be our next Dev Journal. See you next week![/b]

notes.title: Dev Journal #3 – This can be useful or Scavenge 101.
notes.content:
[h1]Hail brave defenders of the castle![/h1]

Welcome to yet another [b]Dev Journal[/b]!

Last Thursday you could read about fighting the enemy patrols and why you shouldn’t do it. This is one of the most important factors in every survival game, and especially significant in [b]Gloria Victis: Siege[/b] – the game is fun as long as enemies pose danger.

That’s why [b]every expedition to the ruined city to scavenge is so full of emotions[/b].

But why should you explore an area formerly known as a city?

[h3]Welcome to the Scavenge 101![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/3a57d8be84cd5c1c57b12a26352e27d22d66af98.gif[/img]

That’s right. [i]It’s not stealing if the city is destroyed[/i], the soldiers are patrolling the city and you are the sole (at the beginning) [b]survivor providing help for the whole castle[/b] defenders and civilians.

[b]Each night you can exit your shelter[/b], armed or not, and look around the place your hero knew since he was little. But you are the one controlling him.

You, [b]the player[/b], can check every alley, corner, and nook for the visible prompt, that something interesting is there. It can be food, utilities necessary for upgrading your castle, ingredients for healing ointments, and even [u][b]arms[/b][/u]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/889e3d84d087bfcead3ce2609679f69d5e5600f1.png[/img]

I got carried away a little.

But yes, you can find weapons – bows and melee weapons for the soldiers and axes for civilians. [b]You will have to manage the noise you’re making [/b]– how quickly you move and search containers (more about this in upcoming Dev Journals).

Like in every survival game, during your scavenger hunt you’ll have to [b]take care of your inventory[/b]. There’s not much our hero can carry with him, so every visit has to be thought out. Do you need another stack of wood, or maybe take another batch of vegetables?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/1bd00dc097ba2a845be760f8ef996d6141e67c03.gif[/img]

How much can your hero carry with him? It depends on the [b]perks[/b] he (or she) has!

Some will be stronger, some are cowards. One of the first survivors you will meet is a [b]thief [/b]. What’s his perk? It’s “[i]thief[/i]” of course. He knows how to stack items inside his pockets, that’s why he will have more inventory space than your first survivor.

[b]What perks we have for you? This will be our next Dev Journal topic![/b]

notes.title: Dev Journal #2 – To fight, or not to fight?
notes.content:
Hello Community!

Welcome to another [b]Dev Journal[/b]! Last week you could read about the main goal standing behind [b]Gloria Victis: Siege[/b] – to let you [b]experience surviving an invasion of a medieval castle[/b]. Such a unique approach requires equally uncommon methods. It quickly comes to one especially significant question:

[h3]To fight, or not to fight?[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/d97d9eef14951c822b42238f106cb213e058174e.jpg[/img]

We want you to think about [b]how to survive the siege[/b]. But when we were prototyping the mechanics of periodic enemy assaults, any solution in which the civilians controlled by a player had to stand the invaders on the walls, the focus has instantly moved from survival to getting efficient in combat.

The player was encouraged to master the means to defeat the enemy in a fight, not to figure out how to stay alive – which was not playing well with our core assumptions. On top of that, the [b]enemy who can be simply beaten is not scary[/b] – such an enemy becomes a mere obstacle, not a real threat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/17908c761dc66b3fdade6738244518955bcb9a01.png[/img]

That’s why, in the end, we’ve had to [b]separate the defenders from civilians[/b]. You command a group of civilians, the very last survivors of a well-prospering city below which has been plundered by the raiders from the North. These people aren’t warriors and they won’t stand a chance against the invaders in face-to-face combat. That’s what soldiers do, though, and you’ve got to make sure they survive long enough.

There’s a small group of the castle guards standing against overwhelming enemy forces. If their [b]Bastion[/b] falls, the invaders will break into the castle and [b]slay everyone inside[/b]. If you’re about to survive the siege, you’ll have to support the soldiers with weapons and provisions, and the wounded and sick will demand your care too. This solution surely adds to the experience of surviving in a besieged castle, and we love it already!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/81b5d95510232fcbef61bf82ae00499ab6caab59.jpg[/img]

However, in the time of war where [b]resources are scarce[/b], there will be times when you have to balance between sustaining the soldiers’ strength and taking care of your own survival. You’ll have to go outside, to scavenge the ruins of the fallen city and look for the supplies in the streets patrolled by the enemy scouts.

[b]How will you overcome them – coming next week![/b]

notes.title: Dev Journal #1 – Survive the siege!
notes.content:
Hello Community!

This is the first of the planned Dev Logs in which you will find lots of info about Gloria Victis: Siege and its unique approach, Behind-The-Scenes materials and much more. We’ll do our best to post the journal every Thursday, so stay tuned! Today’s topic:

[h3]What makes Gloria Victis: Siege such a unique experience?[/h3]
At its base, [b]Gloria Victis: Siege[/b] is an experience of surviving an invasion of a medieval castle. We want you to feel the terror when you see the enemy forces assaulting the walls. We want you to feel the weight of choices you’re about to make. We want you to go through the hardships of a complete lockdown – although we’re all getting this one in a kind of AR experience these days.

in short, we want you to think about [i]how to survive[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37186745/3903ccec925c65763b6ca6f8fb9a5275794e6e98.png[/img]

We want you, the player controlling a group of civilians, to experience how hard might it be to fulfill the most basic needs, such as finding edible food or fresh water in the city ruins when your supplies go low. You’ll have to wisely manage your wood, which you can use as a fuel. And since we’re talking about middle ages, you’ll have to face the lack of fridges, and yet to do your best preserve food.

There’s also one important aspect: the mood of your survivors. They’ll have to walk together with the very last soldiers holding the castle. Even though the defenders are often friends or relatives to remaining civilians, there will be times when you’ll have to make sacrifices. Otherwise, neither will survive – but we’ll talk about it next week.

Stay tuned!
